title: Lunceford's manners and his brother Connie
summary: Crouch probes Lunceford's discipline and Crawford talks about his family and his valet brother Connie, a heavy drinker.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: So now, you're saying that the things that Lunsford taught you were --
-- be well dressed, ties tied, shoes polished --
Almost military like, kind of, huh?
Do you think this was a carryover, was a carryover from his being an athletic director?
I don't know what it was a carryover of.
Oh, did you meet many -- any of his family?

Yeah, very nice people, out of Warren, Ohio. He had a brother that could drink as much whiskey as Al Norris and I, by the name of Connie Lunsford. He was a valet. Yes, he really could -- I mean he drank -- he drank pretty heavy. Lunsford used to look at him in disgust. He never would say anything to him. Well, he's dead now also. And I'm still alive, thank God. I'll never take a drink of whiskey in my life, the remainder of my life, and I've been off now quite a number of years, and you couldn't pay me to drink anything with alcohol in it, unless it's medication, something like that that the doctors prescribe.
